seo.og_title: El Marsa Port, Laâyoune: Fresh Seafood & Harbour Life
seo.og_description: Bustling fishing port with daily landings of sardines, octopus and white fish – the best place for authentic Atlantic seafood near Laâyoune.

name: El Marsa Port
hero_subtitle: The economic heart of Laâyoune’s coast: a busy fishing harbour where daily Atlantic catches become the freshest grilled seafood in the Sahara.

overview.title: Where the Ocean Feeds the Sahara
overview.p1: El Marsa Port (Port of Laâyoune / Marsa) is one of the most important fishing harbours in Morocco and a major economic engine for the southern provinces. Every day, coastal and artisanal boats land hundreds of tonnes of fish – sardines, octopus, cuttlefish, sole, and many other Atlantic species.
overview.p2: The port area is lively, practical and authentic. You will see the wholesale fish market, boats unloading, and simple grills where the day’s catch is cooked on the spot. It is the best place near Laâyoune to taste truly fresh seafood.
overview.p3: A visit combines easily with Foum El Oued Beach (very close) and makes a perfect half-day coastal excursion from the city.

moods.title: Best Moments at El Marsa Port
moods.subtitle: The atmosphere changes with the tide of boats and lunch service.

1.title: Landings & Market Energy
1.desc: Arrive early to see boats returning and the wholesale market in full activity. This is the most authentic and photogenic time.

2.title: Fresh Grilled Seafood
2.desc: The simple restaurants and grills around the port serve the catch of the day. Perfect for a relaxed seafood lunch with harbour views.

3.title: Quieter Harbour Walk
3.desc: Activity slows down. A good time for a calm stroll along the waterfront before combining with a beach visit or returning to the city.

food.title: What to Eat at El Marsa Port
food.p1: This is one of the best places in southern Morocco for ultra-fresh seafood at very reasonable prices.
food.li1: Grilled sardines – the classic, simple and delicious local speciality.
food.li2: Fresh octopus, cuttlefish and calamari, often grilled or in simple preparations.
food.li3: White fish (sole, hake, sea bream) of the day, grilled or fried.
food.li4: Seafood platters shared with bread, lemon and salad.
food.li5: Simple mint tea or soft drinks to finish the meal.
food.p2: Most places are casual, no-frills eateries focused on the quality of the fish rather than decoration.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting El Marsa Port

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Grand taxis from Laâyoune city centre take about 25–30 minutes. Many visitors combine the port with Foum El Oued Beach in the same trip.

2.title: Best Time for Photos & Atmosphere
2.desc: Morning landings offer the most activity and authentic scenes. Always ask before photographing people closely.

3.title: What to Expect
3.desc: This is a working commercial port, not a polished tourist marina. Dress modestly, wear comfortable shoes, and be ready for a lively, real harbour atmosphere.

q1.question: Is El Marsa Port open to visitors?
q1.answer: Yes, the surrounding area and many of the simple restaurants are accessible. The wholesale market itself is a working commercial space; observe respectfully.

q2.question: How far is the port from Laâyoune?
q2.answer: Approximately 25–30 kilometres west of the city centre (about 25–30 minutes by taxi).

q3.question: What is the best time to eat at the port?
q3.answer: Lunchtime (12–3 pm) is ideal for the freshest fish. Morning is best if you want to see the boats and market activity.

q4.question: Is the seafood expensive?
q4.answer: No. Portside grills and simple restaurants offer very good value for extremely fresh fish and seafood.

q5.question: Can I combine the port with Foum El Oued Beach?
q5.answer: Yes – they are very close to each other and make an excellent half-day or full-day coastal outing from Laâyoune.
